name: PyTorch
tagline: A tensor and machine-learning framework with Python APIs and native CPU and GPU implementations.
hook: Explains why a README edit can rebuild CI images and why one page of check results can make a failing PR look green.
summary: PyTorch's AGENTS.md points to CLAUDE.md for contribution policy, native builds, tests, CUDA, and ghstack. Many rules name a failure that normal Python or Git habits can cause, then give the repository-specific command instead.

techniques.title: Expose the cost hidden behind a documentation edit
techniques.body: The Docker directory is content-hashed as a whole, so even its README participates in rebuild decisions. The guide warns against touching that directory during an upstream build outage unless a rebuild is intended.
techniques.quote:
Any file change inside `.ci/docker/` (including the README)
changes the hash and triggers a full Docker image rebuild.

techniques.title: Distinguish intentional detached HEAD from a missing branch
techniques.body: The Git section treats detached HEAD as part of ghstack, while ordinary branch work should branch first. The subsequent workflow preserves metadata trailers and routes submission through ghstack.
techniques.quote:
If HEAD is detached, that is intentional (the ghstack workflow). Do NOT
  create a new branch; commit directly onto the current detached HEAD.

techniques.title: Name a verification result that can be falsely green
techniques.body: A PR can have more check runs than one API page returns. The file replaces a fixed-size check-runs request with gh pr checks so omitted results are not interpreted as success.
techniques.quote:
A PR has hundreds of check-runs, so a single
  `check-runs?per_page=100` call silently truncates and makes red look green.

techniques.title: Reject a lint suppression that removes a runtime check
techniques.body: The S101 guidance explains that Python optimization strips assert statements. It shows an explicit conditional and AssertionError replacement, then preserves the original message and NaN-sensitive comparison semantics.
techniques.quote:
# Bad - silences the rule; the check disappears under `python -O`
assert isinstance(x, Foo)  # noqa: S101

# Good
if not isinstance(x, Foo):
    raise AssertionError(f"expected Foo, got {type(x)}")

techniques.title: Edit type-stub templates rather than their products
techniques.body: The type-stub section names .pyi.in as the editable source for generated .pyi files. The distinction is stated directly so a type fix survives regeneration.
techniques.quote:
Many `.pyi` files are generated from corresponding `.pyi.in` templates. Always
edit the `.pyi.in` file, not the generated `.pyi`.

steal: Name changes whose operational cost is larger than their diff suggests.
Detect the repository's workflow before applying generic Git habits.
Document pagination limits that can conceal verification failures.
Explain runtime semantics behind lint rules instead of recommending suppression.
outline: Fixing B950 line too long in multi-line string blocks
